versusHEAD.reading: Except for the two removal-only edits above, the whole HEAD delta was already present in the pre-012A baseline (uncommitted OBS-007 work frozen before 012A). In browser.ts that delta is Playwright/CDP glue: verifyBrowserPreferences (chrome://version and chrome://prefs-internals probe), mainDocumentTransition, startup video guard wiring and launchPersistentContext for the guided profile. Its non-Playwright logic is delegated to covered siblings: observedBootstrap (BootstrapPageGuard, boundedStartup), appVideoOwnership (validateAppVideoPath), passwordControl (createPasswordControl) and scratchLayout (profile preparation, preference assertions, confinement). Small inline expressions remain, but none is a standalone pure function: a deadline clamp Math.max(now+1, Math.min(deadline, now+5000)), an error-description-to-code mapping, and realpath/lstat checks on the produced video. child.ts wraps launch with prepareBrowserProfile from scratchLayout. guidedMain.ts adds a call to assertObservedBrowserStartup from compat/runtime-versions.

failed.analysis: The fault injection renames Default and then symlinks it while the real Chromium is running. Chromium recreated Default between the two calls, so the injection threw before returning a context and the product never saw the redirected profile. This is a test-harness race, not a product refusal failure (inferred from the error site).

findings.severity: MEDIUM (evidence gap against R4 C2, not a product defect)
findings.summary: No studio-runner tier executes src/run/guidedMain.ts. Its only executing consumers are backend ITs, which were not run here. The unit-tier exclusion of guidedMain.ts therefore has no runner-tier compensating proof. Owner decision needed (@architect/@qa): accept the backend guided ITs as the C2 proof for guidedMain (and run them on the final tree), or add a runner fixtures test that starts dist/run/guidedMain.js. Not done here, because adding a test is outside 'fix genuine defects'.

The direct process-entry block of src/run/child.ts (v8-ignored since before 012A) is never executed by any runner tier. Fixtures import startChild through wrapper entries instead of forking child.js itself.

The vitest.config.ts exclusion comment says the three files 'run only as child processes in the fixtures tier'. In fact browser.ts is also imported in-process by 8 fixtures files (plus 4 via preparedBrowser.ts), and guidedMain.ts does not run in the fixtures tier at all (F1). The config was not edited (do-not-edit for lanes).

The fixtures tier's globalSetup rebuilds studio-runner/dist. During this lane a backend guided IT in another session was spawning from studio-runner/dist, so the two can interfere. Serialize fixtures-tier runs with backend guided ITs.
